correctness.rationale: For uniform random priorities on finite trees, cavity vacancy probabilities on path branches satisfy f_r(t)=sum_{j=0}^r(-t)^j/j!, f_r prime=-f_{r-1}. Adding one private leaf to a path center changes center and leaf contributions by 1-int f_a f_b, while each arm contributes iterated convolution of t f_other. Summing branch lengths gives bivariate generating function N(x,y)/((1-x)(1-y)) with numerator a three-term explicit integral. Coefficients are exact rational integrals bounded 2^(p+q)/(p!q!), proving boundary and bulk limits with factorial remainders. Nonconstant N(x,1) coefficients alternate with strictly decreasing positive magnitudes c_j; hence E_a=sum_{j<=a}(-1)^(j+1)c_j has unique minimum a=2 and E2=(1-5exp(-2))/2; bulk limit=(1-exp(-2))/4. An independent finite first-arrival recursion exactly matches all 16 (a,b) pairs 0..3 with rational coefficient sums, and a separate printed script has 62 package checks. Neither finite test substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A single pendant branch is the simplest deviation from the path, which is known to minimize random greedy independent-set expectation among trees. Its order-one excess is invisible in the leading density, making the complete oscillatory boundary profile, strictly minimizing depth two, and universal bulk value mathematically informative sensitivity invariants. Exact coefficients and factorial convergence go beyond the qualitative path-minimality theorem.
